checkpoints.name: fee_dimensions_and_custody
exit_criteria: Every authoritative fee amount carries an exact asset and custody owner.
Only protocol-owned fee credits fund executable treasury, reward, buyback, and dust allocations.
Per-asset conservation and mixed-asset partition invariance pass on Python and every promoted implementation.
Canonical codecs, roots, patches, receipts, and migration rules are versioned for the new fee values.
nonclaims: P4B4 exact settlement validation does not close fee denomination or custody.
Scalar fee arithmetic tests do not establish executable custody conservation.

checkpoints.name: production_nonce_policy
exit_criteria: The production context uses a closed nonce-policy type and cannot admit the legacy nonce-free variant.
The mount derives and receipt-binds the nonce policy from authenticated deployment configuration.
Identical nonce-free replay fails closed on every production entry point.
nonclaims: A frozen Boolean does not establish policy authority.
Nonce-free compatibility may remain only in a structurally isolated test or differential profile.

checkpoints.name: evidence_recomputation
exit_criteria: Decision derivation recomputes support material and every budget count from retained exact inputs and traces.
No cached producer field independently authorizes a receipt or budget decision.
One mutation-killing negative exists for every evidence field.
nonclaims: Controlled constructors alone do not protect Python values from hostile same-process mutation.
Shape validation of a digest does not prove its semantic preimage.

checkpoints.name: commit_history_and_nullifiers
exit_criteria: Reference publication history validates every adjacent pre-root and successor-root edge from an authenticated checkpoint.
Sequence, previous-publication root, snapshot version, and deployment identity are publication-bound.
Nullifiers are atomically persisted and uniqueness-enforced, or a checked redundancy theorem removes them from commit authority.
Splice, reorder, deletion, truncation, ABA, cross-version, concurrent duplicate, and recovery tests pass.
nonclaims: The immutable reference store is not a production datastore or crash-recovery proof.
Nonce advancement does not by itself prove every declared nullifier redundant.

checkpoints.name: authenticated_context_and_proof_gate
exit_criteria: Only an authenticated shell can construct the context witness from a verified ledger header and deployment policy.
The context and receipt bind chain or deployment identity, policy epoch, consensus time authority, and configuration root.
The five-file settlement proof recomputation lane accepts every expected-valid packet and rejects minimized stale or mismatched packets.
The first failing expected-valid packet is minimized and retained as a regression.
nonclaims: Canonical context encoding proves which values were used, not who authorized them.
The demonstrated proof-gate failure is expected-valid crash or rejection; unsound acceptance has not been demonstrated.

checkpoints.name: total_debt_supply_cap
exit_criteria: Python minting guards total debt before plus debt delta against the system supply cap.
The permanent invariant includes total debt less than or equal to the system supply cap.
Tau derives max-supply validity from total debt, Stability Pool debt, debt delta, and the cap instead of accepting an unbound Boolean.
Python, Rust, Tau, ESSO, proof guests, and independent economic oracles pass cap-minus-one, cap, and cap-plus-one vectors with Stability-Pool-heavy debt.
nonclaims: Supply conservation alone does not establish compliance with a configured supply cap.
ZUSD-P0 is separate from the spot P4B4 checkpoint and is mandatory before an all-value M6 claim.

findings.title: cross_asset_fee_unit_collapse
findings.invariant: Amounts denominated in distinct assets cannot be added or carried as one authoritative scalar without an explicit authenticated conversion.
minimal_witness: One settlement contains a fill fee of 100 units of asset A and a fill fee of 1 unit of asset C.
_total_settlement_fees_v1 and _derive_plan_v1 produce the scalar total 101.
FCISFeeAllocationV1 and CommittedFeeAccumulatorStateV1 retain no asset dimension, so allocation and dust have no unique denomination.
required_repair: Introduce canonical per-asset fee totals, allocations, and dust entries.
Derive each fee asset from the exact admitted intent and fill lineage.
Version every affected schema, codec, state root, patch, effect, receipt, and migration.

required_regression_families.obligation: Mixed input assets never share allocation or dust state.
Allocating disjoint-asset batches together equals canonical per-asset merge of separate allocations.
Python and every promoted implementation produce identical per-asset bytes and roots.

findings.scope_nonclaim: The witness establishes dimensional ambiguity in the unmounted FCIS fee plan; it does not allege a currently mounted external payout.

findings.title: total_fee_split_exceeds_protocol_custody
findings.invariant: Executable fee allocation per asset must equal value actually credited to protocol custody, with every source and destination owner explicit.
minimal_witness: A fill pays a total fee of 100 units and protocol_fee_paid is 10 units.
Settlement replay removes or credits only the 10-unit protocol share while FCIS fee allocation is derived from the 100-unit total.
Executing the allocation would spend 90 units retained for LPs or unrelated protocol custody.
required_repair: Derive distributable fees from protocol_fee_paid grouped by asset.
Represent source custody, destination custody, asset, amount, rounding, and retained dust in the commit plan.
If allocation is analytics-only, remove it from executable commit authority and give it a non-authoritative type.

required_regression_families.obligation: Protocol shares at 0, 1, 9999, and 10000 bps conserve protocol custody per asset.
The LP-retained fee remainder cannot fund treasury, rewards, buyback, or dust.
Trader, recipient, pool, LP, and protocol-recipient aliases do not create or double-spend custody.

findings.scope_nonclaim: Exploitability is conditional on a shell treating the unmounted fee allocation as executable authority.

findings.title: multi_vault_total_supply_cap_bypass
findings.invariant: total_debt_before plus debt_delta must not exceed max_debt_supply, and free_debt plus Stability Pool debt must equal total debt.
minimal_witness: Configure max_debt_supply and max_debt_per_vault to 20000000 units.
Start with vault debts 15000000 and 4000000, free debt 1000000, and Stability Pool debt 18000000.
Mint a 2000000 debt delta into the second vault; the current free-debt guard passes while total debt becomes 21000000.
Supply conservation still passes, so the missing total-debt cap invariant does not reject the successor.
required_repair: Guard _total_debt(state) plus debt_delta against max_debt_supply_e8.
Add total_debt less than or equal to max_debt_supply_e8 to permanent invariants.
Make Tau derive the cap relation from typed inputs rather than trust an externally supplied max_supply_ok Boolean.
Regenerate and parity-check every runtime, formal, and proof implementation.

required_regression_families.obligation: Cap-minus-one, cap, and cap-plus-one vectors pass or reject correctly with most debt in the Stability Pool.
Python, Rust, Tau, ESSO, proof guests, and independent oracle agree on total debt and cap outcomes.
Deposit-to-SP followed by mint cannot bypass the system cap.

findings.scope_nonclaim: This is a separate zUSD P0 blocker and is not closed by the unmounted spot FCIS work.

findings.title: nonce_free_production_profile_representable
findings.invariant: Every production signed intent batch must advance complete replay state under an authenticated, receipt-bound nonce policy.
minimal_witness: Construct FCISStepExecutionContextV1 with require_all_nonces false.
Submit a nonempty batch whose intents all omit nonces.
_validate_and_apply_intent_nonce_batch_admitted_observed_v5 accepts and returns the unchanged nonce state; an identical replay has no nonce memory.
required_repair: Replace the generic Boolean with a closed production or test-only nonce-policy type.
Make the legacy nonce-free constructor unreachable from production admission and mount modules.
Bind the derived policy profile into receipts and deployment configuration.

required_regression_families.obligation: An identical nonce-free intent replay is rejected on every production entry point.
Production modules cannot import or construct the legacy nonce-free policy.
The legacy two-Boolean truth table is preserved only in isolated differential evidence.

findings.scope_nonclaim: The current FCIS path is unmounted; exploitability depends on a future mount admitting the unsafe profile.

findings.title: reference_publication_history_not_chained
findings.invariant: Every publication after an authenticated checkpoint must consume the exact previous successor under one sequence, version, and deployment chain.
minimal_witness: Construct valid bundle A from S0 to S1 and unrelated valid bundle B from T0 to T1 where S1 differs from T0.
Construct ReferenceCommitStoreV1 with current_state T1 and publications A then B.
_revalidate_store_v1 validates each bundle and only compares current_state with B's successor, so the spliced history is accepted.
required_repair: Bind sequence number, expected pre-root, next root, previous-publication root, snapshot version, and chain or deployment identity.
Validate every adjacent edge from an authenticated genesis or checkpoint, or use a checked append-only accumulator.
Make retry classification depend on the authenticated chain, not global membership of an unchained bundle root.

required_regression_families.obligation: Unrelated valid bundle histories cannot be spliced.
Reorder, middle deletion, truncation, fork insertion, ABA, and cross-version mutations fail closed.
Restart and retry preserve one authenticated head and publication sequence.

findings.scope_nonclaim: The defect is in an unmounted reference oracle and does not establish corruption of a production datastore.

findings.title: declared_nullifiers_not_applied
findings.invariant: Every replay atom included in commit authority is atomically uniqueness-enforced, or is removed after a checked proof of redundancy.
minimal_witness: _derive_replay_v1 creates one NullifierRecordV1 for every sender and intent identifier.
ReplayUpdateV1 includes nullifiers in the commit plan.
_apply_patch_atoms_v1 applies nonce advances but has no nullifier state, duplicate check, or compare-and-replace operation.
required_repair: Persist nullifiers atomically, commit them into authoritative state, and enforce uniqueness during compare-and-swap; or
Prove from nonce and intent-ID semantics that duplicate nullifiers are unreachable in every supported profile, then remove nullifiers from executable authority.

required_regression_families.obligation: Two concurrent bundles with one nullifier cannot both publish.
Restart, truncation, restore, and retry cannot lose or duplicate nullifier enforcement.
Higher-nonce reuse, compatibility profiles, and proof-mediated paths match the selected nullifier design.

findings.scope_nonclaim: A concrete live exploit has not been established because nonce checks may make some duplicates unreachable; redundancy is not yet proved.

findings.title: receipt_evidence_not_fully_recomputed
findings.invariant: Receipt-bound support and budget evidence must be freshly derived from retained exact inputs and traces at the authority boundary.
minimal_witness: Mutate support_root, support_set_commitment, state_read_count, context_read_count, canonical_input_bytes, or witness_bytes on an FCISStepEvaluationEvidenceV1 after construction.
_revalidate_evaluation_v1 recomputes context, command, state, snapshot, and root fields but omits those support and count fields.
_budget_violation_v1 then trusts the retained counts, allowing corrupted evidence to influence admission.
required_repair: Retain exact traces and support material and recompute every evidence field during decision derivation.
Derive receipt and budget decisions directly from the fresh result.
Keep no cached producer field as an independent authorization source.

required_regression_families.obligation: Each evidence field has an independent rehashed mutation that reaches semantic re-evaluation and fails closed.
Budget-minus-one, budget, and budget-plus-one traces use freshly computed counts.
Same-shape support roots, sets, versions, and traces cannot be substituted across candidates.

findings.scope_nonclaim: The witness assumes hostile or compromised same-process mutation and does not allege a remote constructor bypass.

findings.title: canonical_context_without_authenticated_origin
findings.invariant: Time, fee policy, deployment policy, settlement mode, and replay policy must come from one authenticated ledger and deployment context that callers cannot construct.
minimal_witness: FCISSettlementExecutionContextV1 and FCISStepExecutionContextV1 admit exact canonical values for now, fee recipient, fee share, mode, quote policy, nonce policy, and snapshot version.
The values contain no verified header witness, chain or deployment identity, policy epoch, or configuration root.
Canonical encoding proves which caller-supplied values were used but does not establish their authority.
required_repair: Introduce a controlled authenticated execution-context witness.
Derive it only from a verified ledger header, authenticated consensus time, deployment configuration root, policy epoch, chain or deployment identity, and authority proof.
Bind the authenticated context root and policy epoch into every receipt and commit bundle.

required_regression_families.obligation: API or proof input cannot choose time, fee recipient, fee share, nonce policy, or settlement mode.
The same command and context bytes cannot replay across chain or deployment identities.
Rollback, forward jump, stale oracle, and LP-age boundaries use authenticated consensus time.

findings.scope_nonclaim: No production mount is present; the finding records a missing premise that must be closed before mounting.

findings.title: expected_valid_settlement_proof_recompute_failure
findings.invariant: Every expected-valid settlement certificate must recompute and validate deterministically, while every stale or mismatched witness must reject.
minimal_witness: The recorded five-file settlement proof recomputation lane exits nonzero on its expected-valid corpus.
The demonstrated failure class is a crash or rejection of expected-valid material during recomputation.
No minimized witness currently demonstrates acceptance of a mismatched or stale proof.
required_repair: Run the exact five-file lane with -x -vv and retain the first failing packet, stdout, stderr, and toolchain binding.
Minimize the expected-valid packet and identify normalization, event, batch-reference, strong-replay, certificate, wrapper, or test-infrastructure divergence.
Retain positive expected-valid and negative stale or mismatched vectors after repair.

required_regression_families.obligation: Every canonical expected-valid packet is accepted without process escape.
Command, pre-root, post-root, effects, event, batch reference, witness, and strong-replay substitutions reject.
No weak or stale validator can substitute for the strong recomputation path.

findings.scope_nonclaim: This ledger does not claim unsound proof acceptance; current evidence demonstrates expected-valid crash or rejection.

global_nonclaims: This ledger is documentation and does not repair, mount, release, or certify any authority path.
M5-P4B4 remains an unmounted exact-strong-validator checkpoint.
No production datastore linearizability, crash recovery, external delivery, Rust parity, proof-guest parity, or all-value conservation claim is made.
All listed checkpoints and ZUSD-P0 must close with source-pinned evidence before an all-value M6 claim can begin.
